description:
RE-TESTED at main a3a9761d1209165e5230625b9347cf6b0ad09b83
(2026-09-02). `Enum.reduce/2` still fails over a non-empty Map, but
the symptom differs by execution path.

## Reproducer

    fn main() do
      map = %{2 => :two, 1 => :one}
      dbg(Enum.reduce(map, fn ({k, _v}, {ak, av}) -> {ak + k, av} end))
    end

Elixir exits 0 and prints:

    {3, :one}

Current fz results:

- interp: exit 1:
  `fz panic: "Enum.EmptyError"`
- run: exit 134:
  `fz_ref_load_atom: ExpectedTag { expected: ValueKind(15), found: ValueKind(3) }`
- build: compilation succeeds, but the built program exits 134 with the
  same `fz_ref_load_atom` tag mismatch.

Do not assume one shared failure mechanism from the old interpreter-only
`Enum.EmptyError` description. Establish why the first-element state is lost
or misclassified on each backend and make the public operation agree across
all three.

## Controls

At the same commit, this program succeeds on interp, run, and build:

    fn main() do
      map = %{2 => :two, 1 => :one}
      dbg(Enum.reduce(map, 0, fn ({k, _v}, acc) -> acc + k end))
      dbg(Enumerable.reduce(map, {:cont, []}, fn (pair, acc) ->
        {:cont, [pair | acc]}
      end))
    end

Output on every path:

    3
    {:done, [{2, :two}, {1, :one}]}

Therefore the live scope is the no-explicit-accumulator bridge; Map's direct
Enumerable callback and public `Enum.reduce/3` remain working controls.

## Fixture state

`fz_f98_map_reduce` and `enum_tier0` are still deferred on every path and
their source headers cite the obsolete ticket `fz-bfh.3`.

The old `enum_tier0` statement that skipping this line next reaches fz-k22 is
also stale: with only this Map `reduce/2` line removed, all three paths exit 0
and print all remaining expected values. They also emit
`warning[type/no-matching-clause]` at `runtime:Enum.fz:267`; because the fixture
has no diagnostics golden, do not describe it as green until that separately
scoped warning is resolved or explicitly owned.

## Decidable checks

- The reproducer exits 0 and prints `{3, :one}` on interp, run, and build.
- The reduce/3/direct-Enumerable control retains the exact output above on all
  three paths.
- Remove the three deferrals from `fz_f98_map_reduce`; all three matrix trials
  pass.
- Remove obsolete `fz-bfh.3` and `fz-k22` claims from affected fixture
  documentation and record only verified live blockers.
- `cargo test --test fixture_matrix map_enumerable -- --test-threads=1`
  remains 3/3 passing.
- Full library and fixture-matrix suites pass at baseline or better, with no
  new controlled warnings.

comments.text: RE-TEST AFTER fz-kdt.120 (2026-09-03): fixtures2/behavior/fz_f98_map_reduce.fz -- whose three matrix doors were deferred with the reason "Enum.reduce/2 over Map raises Enum.EmptyError" -- turns GREEN on interp, run and build under 120's prototype (measured by two independent reviews). If that fixture is this ticket's reproducer, 120 fixes the interp half (the empty-list @spec binding produced the phantom EmptyError path); the JIT/AOT fz_ref_load_atom tag mismatch must be re-tested separately.

title: Enum.reduce/2 over a non-empty Map fails: interp raises Enum.EmptyError; JIT/AOT abort on the seed-state tag
